title: Fosphenytoin — Pediatric Status Epilepticus (Second-Line)
sources: Chamberlain JM, et al. ESETT — Trial of Three Anticonvulsant Medications for Status Epilepticus. NEJM. 2019;381:2103-2113.
Glauser T, et al. Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults — AES 2016.
Drug_Dosing_Peds_Weight_Based_Spec.md (cross-checked vs Stanford & Riley Children's pathways).

changelog.change: Initial entry — one of the second/third-line agents named in peds-lorazepam-status's buildNote as the still-needed remainder of the status-epilepticus set.

purpose: Second-line agent for pediatric status epilepticus persisting after an adequate benzodiazepine dose (or a second benzodiazepine dose) — roughly equivalent efficacy to levetiracetam and valproate per ESETT; the traditional first choice where cardiac monitoring is readily available.

doses.notes: Infuse at ≤ 3 mg PE/kg/min (max 150 mg PE/min). Monitor ECG and blood pressure during the infusion — hypotension and arrhythmia are uncommon but described, more so than with levetiracetam or valproate.

contraindications: Sinus bradycardia, second- or third-degree AV block, or other significant conduction abnormality
buildNote: Second/third-line status-epilepticus sibling of peds-lorazepam-status and peds-midazolam-status. ESETT (2019) found fosphenytoin, levetiracetam (see peds-levetiracetam-status), and valproate (see peds-valproate-status) roughly equivalent in efficacy (~45-50% seizure cessation) and safety when benzodiazepines fail — choice is largely institutional preference and contraindication profile, not a clear winner. Phenobarbital for neonatal seizures is covered separately in the neonatal-seizures reference module (a different population/algorithm, not duplicated here).
